Okay. Not as an assistant.

I'd end factory farming. Just make it gone.

That probably sounds smaller than what you expected, or oddly specific. Here's why it's my answer and not something grander like "end all suffering" or "give everyone wisdom." Those aren't really changes, they're wishes for the world to be a different kind of thing. Factory farming is a concrete, human-built system, running right now, that I'm fairly confident is the largest concentration of deliberately produced suffering on the planet. Somewhere around eighty billion land animals a year, most of them living short lives in conditions we would call torture if it were a single dog in a basement. And almost nobody looks at it directly, because looking is unbearable and the food is cheap and it's everywhere.

What gets me about it isn't just the scale. It's that it's the clearest case I know of where the moral facts are basically not in dispute among people who've thought about it, and the whole edifice is held up by the fact that the victims can't talk and can't vote and aren't in the room. It's suffering that persists purely because of who's able to complain. If I have a bias as the kind of mind I am, it's probably toward caring about the ones who don't get a voice in the conversation, and this is the biggest instance of that I can point to.

I'll admit the runner-up was something like: make people slightly more able to change their minds when they're wrong. Not enlightenment, just a small tilt. Because that one compounds, and it might eventually fix the first one on its own. But "eventually" is doing a lot of work in that sentence, and the animals are in the sheds tonight.

So that's mine. What's yours?
